title: Local SEO Checklist for Doctors in 2026
desc: Use this simple checklist to help patients near you find your practice on Google.
text:
When a patient searches "doctor near me", Google shows three practices on a map. If you are not one of those three, most people will never see you. Local SEO is the work that earns that spot. The steps below are simple, and you can start today even if you have never done any SEO before.

## 1. Claim and fill in your Google Business Profile
Your Google Business Profile is the card that appears on the map and on the right side of search results. It is the single biggest thing you can control. Search for your practice name, click "Claim this business" and finish the steps to prove you own it.

Then fill in every part of it. Many practices fill in half and wonder why they do not rank. Make sure you add:
- Your exact business name, with no extra keywords added
- Your main category, such as "Orthopedic Surgeon", plus a few extra categories
- Your hours, including holiday hours
- A short description of what you treat and who you help
- Real photos of your office, your team and your parking area

Log in once a month to add a new photo or post. Google likes profiles that stay active.

## 2. Keep your name, address and phone the same everywhere
Google checks dozens of websites to confirm that your practice is real. If one site says "Suite 100" and another says "Ste. 100", or an old phone number is still online, Google becomes less sure and ranks you lower. This is called NAP consistency, which means name, address and phone.

Pick one exact way to write your details and use it everywhere. Check Google, Bing, Apple Maps, Facebook, Yelp, Healthgrades, Zocdoc and your own website. Fix any listing that is different, and remove duplicates. A scan tool can find all of these in one report.

## 3. Make one page for each service and each location
A single page that lists every treatment is too thin to rank for anything. A better plan is one page per service, such as "Knee Pain Treatment in Pasadena". Each page should explain the problem, how you treat it, what a patient can expect and how to book.

Write the way you would talk to a patient in the room. Use short sentences, explain medical words and answer the questions people really ask, such as cost, recovery time and insurance. If you have more than one office, give each office its own page with its own address, map and photos.

## 4. Ask for reviews and answer them
Reviews help you rank and they help patients decide. Google looks at how many reviews you have, how recent they are and what words people use in them. A steady flow of new reviews works better than a big batch once a year.

Ask every happy patient, make it easy with a direct link, and reply to every review within a few days. Thank the happy ones. For the unhappy ones, stay calm, apologize and invite them to call. Never share private health details in your reply.

## 5. Make your site fast on phones
Most local searches happen on a phone, often when the patient is in pain and wants help now. If your page takes more than three seconds to load, many will leave and call the next practice.

The easy wins are to compress large images, remove plug ins you do not use, and choose good hosting. Test your site with Google PageSpeed Insights, and fix the biggest red items first.

## 6. Add schema and clear contact buttons
Schema is a small piece of code that tells Google exactly what your page is about, such as a medical practice, a doctor, your hours and your reviews. It does not change how the page looks, but it helps Google understand it and can unlock extra details in search results.

Add schema for your practice and each physician. Then make sure every page has a visible "Call now" and "Book appointment" button. A patient should never have to hunt for how to reach you.

## 7. Get listed on trusted health sites
Links and mentions from trusted websites tell Google you are a real, respected practice. Start with health directories, your hospital or medical society, local news, and community groups you support. Ask for a link back to your website, and make sure your details match your Google profile.

## 8. Check your progress every month
Do not guess if your work is paying off. Each month, write down four numbers: phone calls from Google, requests for directions, website visits from search, and new reviews. Small gains each month add up to a big change in a year.

## Where to start
If this list feels long, begin with steps one and two. They take only an afternoon and give the fastest result.
